The purpose of this bulletin is to alert substation 
 maintenance staff to defective flanges on hollow support and arcing chamber 
 insulators of air blast circuit breakers 66kv type 3P72- Rade Concar.

In Delta Zone after some years of putting this type
 of circuit breakers in operation, cracks were discovered on the flanges
 connecting the hollow support insulators to the flanges of the air tanks, and
 the hollow support insulators to the arcing chamber insulators. These cracks
 appeared between the stud holes connecting the flanges together.

The flanges of (the hollow insulators) the arcing chamber
insulators and there stud bolts are manufactured from aluminum alloys which
tented to corrode after several years exposure to weather conditions. Cracks are
formed at points, on weak points of the flanges between the holes of the stud
bolts. The cracks (if small) allow air to leak, however if left not repaired may
cause the insulator to explode.

It is recommended defective flanges be replaced with new one
as soon as possible after they have been discovered.

Middle Delta Zone has been successful in manufacturing new
flanges and their stud bolts from copper and have changed most of the aluminum
flanges. These repairs have resulted in good reliable services for several
years. They dont expect further problems in this area.

Procedure for Replacing Cracked Flanges Drawings refer to 
mpis doc no. CB-007-r0

items: A work permit must be issued.

CB must be isolated and proper earthling at the two sides of the CB is
 required.
Safety fence with caution marks around the work area is required.
Cut off the DC voltage.
Wearing safety helmet is required.
Use only fiberglass ladders.
Close the through valve (1 fig 1).

Open the drainage valve (24 fig 1) to drain the air out of the tank and be
 sure that the breaker is free of pressure. The pressure can be read at the
 control pressure gauge placed in the control cubicle.

Personnel carrying out this work should be trained and qualified or
 directly supervised by some one who is.

Mobile crane-Triple sheaved-Sufficient and suitable polypropylene rope to
 lower arcing chambers and hollow support insulators to ground - suitable
 steel shackles.

One set of metric open end box wrenches size range 13 mm to 24 mm,
 Adjustable spanner, One set of screwdrivers and Torque wrench.
Fine file, Fine emery paper, Wipers.

Hammer kg, Hammer 2 kg, Rubber
 hammer, suitable steel punch to drive out studs.
Sufficient numbers of stud bolts used in assembling the flanges.
Tin cans to hold bolts, nuts, studs, washersetc.
Complete set of gaskets (8 gaskets for every pole).

Complete set of flanges (Lower and upper flanges of arcing chambers
 insulators and hollow support insulators.
Electrical disk saw, hand saw.
Petroleum jelly (Vaseline).

Before working ensure the crane operator is fully aware of neighbouring
 apparatus and the safe limits of approach to over head lines or bus-bars.
The mobile crane must be grounded (earthed).

Don't use the mobile crane for the actual lift but attach a rope block and 
use the crane hook as a gin pole

Remove the protective cap at the end of arcing chamber that covers the
 valves (30, 31, 32 fig 2). Use spanner 19
Disconnect the insulating tube (20, 26 fig 2).

With the polypropylene rope blocks hang the arcing chamber with the crane
 hook.

Release the nuts of the 12 stud bolts connecting the lower flange of the
 hollow support insulator to the flange of air tank. Use
 spanner 17

Using the crane hook as a gin pole lower the complete pole (arcing chamber
 and hollow support insulator) till the lower flange of the hollow support
 insulator becomes in your reach to easily handled, then dismantle it. Close
 the tank flange with any provisional cover to prevent ingress of dirt or any
 thing in the tank. Support insulator and arc chamber should be lowered
 slowly as to prevent porcelain from shocks.

To get the flange out of the porcelain of the hollow support insulator,
 hammer at the 3 piece split ring using a rubber hammer to get them out, then
 the flange will be free.

Move the complete pole (arcing chamber and hollow support insulator) aside
 and put it on a wooden base.

Release the 12 stud bolts connecting the upper flange of the hollow
 support insulator and the lower flange of fixed contact base. Use spanner 17

Move the complete arcing chamber with the fixed contact base aside and
 lower it on the wooden base.

Release the 12 stud bolts connecting the lower flange of the arcing
 chamber to the upper flange of fixed contact base. Use spanner 17 and tube
 spanner 17

Hammer at the 3-piece split ring using a rubber hammer to get the flange
 out. If the stud bolts are difficult to release because of the weather
 conditions, saw the 2 studs in the direction of the fixed contact outlet
 valve using a hand saw, then saw the other 10 studs using an electrical disc
 saw.

Hammer at the remaining of the stud bolts using suitable steel punch to
 drive them out from upper flange of fixed contact base.

Exchange the flange with another new one and erect it in its place after
 cleaning the 3 split ring surfaces with fine emery paper.

Erect the lower flange of arc camber to the upper flange of fixed contact
 base with their 12 stud bolts. Use spanner 17

Release the nuts of the 6 stud bolts connecting the base of entire moving
 contact to the upper flange of arcing chamber insulator gradually by half
 turn all
 around 
 Use spanner 19

Pull out this base with entire moving contact exactly parallel to the
 chamber centerline, taking care that the porcelain screen head would not be
 broken. 
 Use spanner 17 and tube spanner 17

To seperate the upper flange of arcing chamber from the porcelain, hammer
 at the 3-piece split ring using a rubber hammer to get them out, then the
 flange will be free.

Replace this flange with a new one, after cleaning the 3 split ring
 surfaces with fine emery paper

Replace the entire moving contact in its place into the arcing chamber and
 tighten the 6 studs. Use spanner 19

Exchange the lower flange of arcing chamber with another new one and erect
 it with the fixed upper flange of the fixed contact base after cleaning the
 3 split ring surfaces with fine emery paper and tighten their 12 studs. Use
 spanner 17

Raise the arcing chamber with complete fixed contact up and erect it to
 the upper flange of the hollow support insulator with their 12 stud .

Raise the complete pole (arcing chamber and hollow support insulator) up
 over the flange of the air tank, then place the new flange with its 3 split
 ring after cleaning them with fine emery paper and erect it to the flange of
 air tank with their 12 stud bolts.

Erect the control insulator on its place and connect all control tubes to
 their previous places. Use spanners 24 and 19
Measure the support column insulation by megger.

Notes: Tighten all nuts with torque wrench to their correct
value.
